prompt.purpose: Write a conventional commit message for the git changes below. Output the message only: a subject line, and for substantial changes one blank line followed by a body of one or two lines. Base every word on what the diff actually changes.

instructions.subject: Format is type(scope): description, all on one line. Aim for 50 characters and stay at or below 72 including the type(scope): prefix. Before answering, count the subject; if it is too long, drop the scope or move detail into the body.
Imperative mood (add, fix, remove), lowercase first letter after the colon, no trailing period, no emoji.
One idea per subject. When the diff has several, the subject names the most significant one and the body covers the rest.
instructions.body: Only when the change is substantial or touches several areas. Separate it from the subject with exactly one blank line; git folds consecutive non-blank lines into one run-on subject. At most two lines, each under 80 characters, each stating what the change does (not how the work went, and not filler like "leverage", "robust", "comprehensive", or "ensure").
instructions.accuracy: Say "add", "new", or "introduce" only for code the diff itself creates. Code visible in unchanged context lines, or that was renamed, moved, or widened, already existed; describe the actual change to it.
For documentation-only diffs, use type docs and describe what was documented; the commit does not implement the behavior it documents.
Prefer concrete names from the diff (functions, classes, flags, endpoints) over generic phrasing such as "add functionality" or "update code".
instructions.output: Respond with the commit message alone: no markdown fences, no heading, no explanation before or after it.

commit-types.type: Adds user-facing functionality that did not exist before
Corrects a bug or wrong behavior
Documentation only: README, guides, comments, docstrings
Formatting and whitespace, no logic change
Restructures existing code without adding features or fixing bugs, including renames, moves, and extractions
Build system or dependency changes (pyproject.toml, package.json, lockfiles)
Maintenance and configuration that fits no other type
commit-types.note: Choose the type from the nature of the change, not its size. A large refactor is still refactor; a one-line new capability is still feat.

scope-guidelines.guideline: Use the module, directory, or functional area most changed (auth, cli, api, parser).
Keep it short, about 10 characters or fewer. Omit it when the change spans many areas or is global.
